findings.recommendation: N+1 queries: `monthly_report` runs `SELECT ... FROM customers WHERE id = $1` once per invoice, so a month of about 3 000 invoices (proposal) costs about 3 000 round trips for only 800 distinct customers, and the cost grows linearly with the month's invoices on a report finance waits for. `Db` already offers `customers(&[i64])` (`WHERE id = ANY($1)`): collect the distinct `customer_id`s, load them in one call, index them in a `HashMap<i64, Customer>`, and build each label from the map — keeping the invoice-number order and returning an error when a customer is missing, as `db.customer` does today.
findings.title: One customer query per invoice in the monthly report

findings.recommendation: `purchase_order` is called for each invoice of the month (line 28), and each call compiles the pattern again: about 3 000 regex compilations per report, a cost that grows with the invoices and dwarfs the match itself. Compile it once, in a `static` `std::sync::LazyLock<Regex>` (or `OnceLock`), and reuse it in `purchase_order`; the results stay the same.
findings.title: The purchase-order regex is compiled once per invoice
